title: Mapping Urban Heat and Cooling Infrastructure
description: High-resolution satellite imagery and machine learning are used to identify white roofs and examine how cooling infrastructure is distributed across communities.
body: This project examines how urban cooling infrastructure is distributed across communities and how that distribution can inform heat-mitigation policy.

High-resolution satellite imagery and machine-learning classification are used to identify features such as white roofs. The resulting spatial evidence can support analysis of infrastructure access, neighborhood differences, and climate adaptation priorities.

title: Energy, Climate, and Environmental Policy
description: This research examines energy governance, climate action, policy implementation, public acceptance, benefit sharing, and pathways toward carbon neutrality.
body: This research program studies how policies, institutions, and communities shape energy and climate transitions.

Projects examine policy implementation, public acceptance, benefit-sharing arrangements, environmental governance, and national pathways toward carbon neutrality using quantitative, qualitative, and computational methods.

title: Environmental Impacts of Data Centers
description: We investigate how data-center development may affect local heat, lighting, land use, electromagnetic fields, and biodiversity across multiple locations.
body: This project investigates the environmental effects associated with the rapid development and operation of data centers.

Satellite imagery, thermal observations, environmental sensors, and comparative case studies are used to assess potential changes in local heat, lighting, land use, electromagnetic fields, and biodiversity.

title: Thermal Imaging and Energy Infrastructure
description: Thermal imagery and drone-based inspection can help evaluate solar infrastructure, building energy systems, and environmental performance.
body: This research explores how thermal imaging can improve the evaluation of energy infrastructure and environmental performance.
Drone-based and remote thermographic observations can reveal temperature patterns, equipment anomalies, and operational characteristics in solar installations and building energy systems.

title: Campus Sustainability Analytics
description: We study sustainability assessment, organizational change, engagement, and performance reporting to support evidence-based campus action.
body: This project studies how colleges and universities assess, organize, and improve campus sustainability.

The work connects performance reporting, stakeholder engagement, organizational change, and program evaluation to support evidence-based institutional action, including work related to the AASHE STARS framework.
